newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rebels blow up Algeria rail track, kill 4 - paper.
newsitem.headline: Rebels blow up Algeria rail track, kill 4 - paper.

text.p: Moslem guerrillas blew up a railway line, derailing a train carrying fuel and killing four people, an Algerian newspaper said on Thursday.

Guerrillas detonated the bomb on Tuesday between Naciria and Tadmait in the province of Tizi-Ouzou, 90 km (55 miles) east of Algiers, causing "significant damage" to the line, the Arab language daily al Khabar said.
The bombing was the latest act of sabotage in the region blamed by the authorities on Moslem rebels, including the destruction of Isser main bridge in Tizi-Ouzou province.
Algerian authorities recently rebuilt the bridge at a cost of 70 million dinars ($1.3 million), officials said.
They blame Moslem militants for sabotage over the past four years which has caused more than $2 billion losses for the North African country's economy.

An estimated 50,000 people have been killed in Algeria's violence pitting Moslem guerrillas against government forces since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a commanding lead.
